title: camelKey on its own, including a mid-word digit
prompt: What does this return? Read it — do not run it.

given.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
---
{
  a: camelKey("user_id"),
  b: camelKey("full_name"),
  c: camelKey("item_2_id"),
  d: camelKey("already")
}

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
---
{
  a: camelKey("user_id"),
  b: camelKey("full_name"),
  c: camelKey("item_2_id"),
  d: camelKey("already")
}

explanation.approach: Splitting on `_` and capitalizing the first letter of every part after the first — a key with no underscore at all just comes back unchanged, which is what `camelKey("already")` shows.
